definition_en: a musical instrument with strings, played with the fingers or a pick
core_image: 手指拨过木吉他的六根琴弦
scene: 他每晚都弹吉他。He plays the guitar every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 guitar 是「吉他」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每晚都弹吉他。

senses.title: Stringed instrument
senses.definition: a musical instrument with strings and a long neck
senses.definitionCN: 带弦和长琴颈的乐器
senses.example: He plays the guitar every evening.
senses.why: This is the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最通用的义项。

senses.title: Electric guitar
senses.definition: a guitar whose sound is made louder by electricity
senses.definitionCN: 靠电力放大声音的吉他
senses.example: The band used two electric guitars.
senses.why: The electric form became a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 电声形式独立成一个义项。

senses.title: Guitar music
senses.definition: music played on a guitar, especially in a band
senses.definitionCN: 用吉他演奏的音乐，尤指乐队中
senses.example: Their songs are full of guitar.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的歌里充满吉他演奏。
senses.why: The instrument name can stand for its sound.
senses.whyCN: 乐器名可以代指它的声音。

intro.en: Guitar comes through French guitare from Latin cithara, from Greek kithara, a lyre.
intro.cn: guitar 经法语 guitare 来自拉丁语 cithara，源头是希腊语 kithara（一种里拉琴）。

items.en: Kithara meant a large lyre.
items.cn: kithara 指一种大型里拉琴。

items.en: Cithara named the same instrument.
items.cn: cithara 指同一种乐器。

items.en: Guitare named a stringed instrument.
items.cn: guitare 指一种弦乐器。

items.en: Guitar named the modern six-string instrument.
items.cn: guitar 指现代六弦乐器。

items.en: Electric guitars added a new sense.
items.cn: 电吉他带来了新的义项。

note.en: Guitar is compared with look-alike words and words for instruments.
note.cn: 把 guitar 与形近词以及表示乐器的词作比较。

entries.definition: the fact of having done wrong
a large area of sea partly enclosed
a sticky substance or chewing sweet
a stringed instrument with a round body
a object used to make music

normalIntro.en: Guitar is a Greek lyre reborn as six strings in wood and wire.
normalIntro.cn: guitar 是希腊里拉琴的转世，化作木与弦上的六根琴弦。

normal.en: She plays the guitar well.
He bought an acoustic guitar.
The electric guitar was loud.
A string broke on my guitar.
The song has a long guitar solo.
normal.cn: 这首歌有一段很长的吉他独奏。

abstract.en: Six strings can hold a whole evening.
abstract.cn: 六根弦，能托住一整个夜晚。

abstract.en: Wood and wire remember every hand.
abstract.cn: 木与弦，记得每一只手。

abstract.en: An old name can learn new music.
abstract.cn: 古老的名字，也能学会新的音乐。

examples.en: He plays the guitar every evening.
The band used two electric guitars.
Their songs are full of guitar.
examples.cn: 他们的歌里充满吉他演奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: guitar 是「吉他」；play the guitar 是弹吉他，electric guitar 是电吉他，acoustic guitar 是木吉他；弹奏者叫 guitarist。

root: 经法语 guitare 来自拉丁语 cithara，再溯至希腊语 kithara（里拉琴）；琴形与名称几经流转，成为今天的六弦吉他。

sensesIntro.en: Guitar means the stringed instrument, its electric form, or guitar music.
sensesIntro.cn: guitar 指吉他、电吉他，或吉他演奏。

core.en: Strings stretched over a wooden body.
core.cn: 绷在木质琴身上的琴弦。

branches.en: Fingers press and pluck six strings.
branches.cn: 手指按住并拨动六根弦。

branches.en: A cable carries the sound to an amp.
A band rides on a wall of chords.
Wood and wire share one shape.
branches.cn: 木吉他与电吉他，共有一个形状。

branches.en: The louder form became its own sound.
branches.cn: 更响的形式，成了自己的声音。

intro.en: Guitar forms plurals and names its players.
intro.cn: guitar 构成复数，并派生出演奏者名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is cithara, from Greek kithara.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 cithara，来自希腊语 kithara。

items.exampleCN: 两位吉他手加入了乐队。

items.meaning: a passage played by guitar alone

definition_en: a weapon that fires bullets or shells, a device that sprays, or to make an engine go faster
core_image: 一把手枪被放回皮套里
scene: 警察收起了枪。The police officer put away the gun.
sceneCN: 这里 gun 是「枪」（第 1 个义项）；句意：警察收起了枪。

senses.title: Firearm
senses.definition: a weapon that fires bullets or shells
senses.definitionCN: 发射子弹或炮弹的武器
senses.example: The police officer put away the gun.
senses.why: This is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的义项。

senses.title: Spraying device
senses.definition: a tool that forces out paint, water, or other material
senses.definitionCN: 喷出油漆、水或其他材料的工具
senses.example: Use the spray gun on the wall.
senses.why: The shape and force of a gun were borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 借用了枪的形状与喷射力。

senses.title: Speed up an engine
senses.definition: to press the accelerator hard and go faster
senses.definitionCN: 猛踩油门使车更快
senses.example: He gunned the engine at the light.
senses.why: The sudden force of firing became speed.
senses.whyCN: 开火般的猛劲引申为加速。

intro.en: Gun appears in Middle English as gunne; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: gun 在中古英语中作 gunne，更早来源不确定。

items.en: The deeper origin of the word is unknown.
items.cn: 这个词更早的来源已不可考。

items.en: Gunne named a large cannon.
items.cn: gunne 指大型火炮。

items.en: Gun named smaller firearms too.
items.cn: gun 也指较小的火器。

items.en: The word named machines that spray.
items.cn: 这个词也指喷射类器械。

items.en: The verb sense of speeding up appeared.
items.cn: 「加速」的动词义出现。

note.en: Gun is compared with look-alike words and words for weapons.
note.cn: 把 gun 与形近词以及表示武器的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sticky substance or chewing sweet
a large area of sea partly enclosed
a long gun fired from the shoulder
a small gun held in one hand

normalIntro.en: Gun is a firearm, a spraying tool, and the verb for sudden speed.
normalIntro.cn: gun 是火器、喷射工具，也是突然加速的动词。

normal.en: The gun was unloaded.
They discussed gun control.
A machine gun fired in the distance.
He used a spray gun on the fence.
She gunned the engine and left.

abstract.en: A tool of force demands careful hands.
abstract.cn: 力量的工具，需要谨慎的手。

abstract.en: Speed borrowed the name of a shot.
abstract.cn: 速度借用了开火的名字。

abstract.en: What can spray can also destroy.
abstract.cn: 能喷射的东西，也能造成破坏。

examples.en: The police officer put away the gun.
Use the spray gun on the wall.
He gunned the engine at the light.

dict_mnemonic.text: gun 是「枪、炮」，也指「喷枪」，动词意为「猛踩油门」；gun control 是枪支管制，machine gun 是机枪，gun down 是枪杀；过去式双写 n 变 gunned。

root: 中古英语作 gunne，原指大型火炮，更早来源不确定；由火炮扩展到各类火器，再借用其形与力指喷射器械，并引申出「加速」。

sensesIntro.en: Gun means a firearm, a spraying tool, or to speed up an engine.
sensesIntro.cn: gun 指枪炮、喷射工具，或猛踩油门加速。

core.en: A metal tube that sends something out fast.
core.cn: 把东西高速射出的金属管。

branches.en: A hand rests on a holstered weapon.
Paint mists from a nozzle.
A foot presses the pedal down.
Weapon and sprayer share a barrel.
Both firing and speeding release force.
branches.cn: 开火与加速，都在释放力量。

intro.en: Gun forms verb parts and a family of weapon words.
intro.cn: gun 构成动词变化以及一组与武器相关的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，来源不确定。

items.example: They were gunning for the prize.

items.meaning: a soldier who fires a gun

definition_en: an informal word for a man, a form of address to a group, or a rope that steadies something
core_image: 街角站着的普通男人
scene: 那个高个子家伙是我朋友。That tall guy is my friend.
sceneCN: 这里 guy 是「家伙」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那个高个子家伙是我朋友。

senses.title: Man
senses.definition: an informal word for a man or boy
senses.definitionCN: 对男人或男孩的非正式称呼
senses.example: That tall guy is my friend.
senses.exampleCN: 那个高个子家伙是我朋友。
senses.why: The everyday sense names an ordinary man.
senses.whyCN: 日常义项指一个普通男人。

senses.title: Group address
senses.definition: a friendly way of speaking to a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 友好地称呼一群人的方式
senses.example: You guys should come with us.
senses.exampleCN: 你们几个该跟我们一起来。
senses.why: The plural became a warm form of address.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式变成了一种亲切的称呼。

senses.title: Steadying rope
senses.definition: a rope used to hold a tent or pole steady
senses.definitionCN: 用来固定帐篷或杆子的绳索
senses.example: He tightened the guy rope.
senses.why: The rope sense comes from a different line of use.
senses.whyCN: 拉索义来自另一条用法线索。

intro.en: Guy began as an English name and passed through the sense of an effigy to mean a man.
intro.cn: guy 最初是英语人名，经「人像、假人」之义转为指男人。

items.en: The name Guy was given to an effigy burned on a feast day.
items.cn: 人名 Guy 被用来称呼节庆日焚烧的人像。

items.en: The effigy sense gave a word for an oddly dressed figure.
items.cn: 人像义又衍生出指衣着古怪之人的说法。

items.en: In American English guy came to mean any man.
items.cn: 在美式英语中，guy 转而泛指任何男人。

items.en: The plural became an informal form of address.
items.cn: 复数形式成为非正式的称呼。

items.en: A separate rope sense grew from the verb of steadying.
items.cn: 表示固定的动词又发展出独立的拉索义。

note.en: Guy is compared with look-alike words and other informal words for a man.
note.cn: 把 guy 与形近词以及其他表示男人的非正式词作比较。

entries.definition: cheerful, or relating to same-sex love
a sticky substance or the flesh around teeth
a man, in British informal use

normalIntro.en: Guy is a relaxed word for a man, a friendly plural address, and a rope that holds things steady.
normalIntro.cn: guy 是对男人的轻松称呼、对一群人的友好招呼，也是固定物体的拉索。

normal.en: That tall guy is my friend.
normal.cn: 那个高个子家伙是我朋友。

normal.en: You guys should come with us.
normal.cn: 你们几个该跟我们一起来。

normal.en: He is a regular guy.
He tightened the guy rope.
The good guys won in the end.

abstract.en: A name for one face becomes a word for any man.
abstract.cn: 一张脸的名字，变成了任何男人的称呼。

abstract.en: A friendly word makes a group feel closer.
abstract.cn: 一个亲切的词，让一群人靠得更近。

abstract.en: Even a rope needs another point to hold.
abstract.cn: 就连绳索，也需要另一个支点。

examples.en: That tall guy is my friend.
examples.cn: 那个高个子家伙是我朋友。

examples.en: You guys should come with us.
examples.cn: 你们几个该跟我们一起来。

examples.en: He tightened the guy rope.

dict_mnemonic.text: guy 是口语里的「家伙、男人」，复数 guys 也用作「你们」的亲切称呼；guy rope 是固定帐篷的拉索。

root: 源自英语人名 Guy，先指节庆中焚烧的人像，再指衣着古怪的人，后在美式英语中泛指男人；拉索义来自表示固定的动词。

sensesIntro.en: Guy means a man informally, a friendly plural address, or a steadying rope.
sensesIntro.cn: guy 指口语中的男人、对一群人的亲切称呼，或起固定作用的拉索。

core.en: An ordinary man standing among others.
core.cn: 站在人群中的一个普通男人。

branches.en: A neighbour waves from the street.
Friends call a group over.
branches.cn: 朋友们招呼一群人过来。

branches.en: A tent line is pulled tight.
One man and a whole group can share the word.
branches.cn: 一个男人和一群人，可以共用这个词。

branches.en: A man and a rope both hold a place.
branches.cn: 人和绳索，都能守住一个位置。

intro.en: Guy forms plurals and rope compounds.
intro.cn: guy 构成复数形式与表示绳索的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word comes from an English name.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，源自一个英语人名。

items.exampleCN: 他们正在用拉索固定帐篷。

items.example: A guy wire supports the mast.

definition_en: something done regularly, the natural behaviour of a plant or animal, or a long garment worn by monks and nuns
core_image: 每天同一时间重复的动作
scene: 每天早起是他的习惯。Getting up early is his habit.
sceneCN: 这里 habit 是「习惯」（第 1 个义项）；句意：每天早起是他的习惯。

senses.title: Repeated action
senses.definition: something that a person does regularly
senses.definitionCN: 一个人经常重复做的事情
senses.example: Getting up early is his habit.
senses.why: A repeated personal action is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 个人重复的动作，是这个词的中心义项。

senses.title: Natural behaviour
senses.definition: the natural way that a plant or animal grows or behaves
senses.definitionCN: 动植物天然的成长或行为方式
senses.example: The plant has a climbing habit.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物有攀爬的习性。
senses.why: The same word names natural growth patterns.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指天然的生长方式。

senses.title: Religious dress
senses.definition: a long loose garment worn by monks or nuns
senses.definitionCN: 修士或修女穿的宽松长袍
senses.example: The monk wore a simple habit.
senses.why: The Latin root also meant dress or bearing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根也兼指衣着与举止。

intro.en: Habit comes from Latin habitus, a condition or dress, from habere, to have.
intro.cn: habit 来自拉丁语 habitus（状况；衣着），源于 habere（拥有）。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold.
items.cn: habere 意为拥有或持有。

items.en: Habitus meant a condition or a way of dressing.
items.cn: habitus 意为状况或衣着方式。

items.en: Abit named a settled manner or dress.
items.cn: abit 指固定的举止或衣着。

items.en: Habit meant a usual manner of acting.
items.cn: habit 指惯常的行为方式。

items.en: It also kept the sense of a monk's dress.
items.cn: 它也保留了修士袍服的含义。

note.en: Habit is compared with look-alike words and words for repeated behaviour.
note.cn: 把 habit 与形近词以及表示重复行为的词作比较。

entries.definition: the natural home of a plant or animal
a usual way of doing something

normalIntro.en: A habit is what a person keeps doing, what a plant keeps doing, or the dress a monk keeps wearing.
normalIntro.cn: habit 是人反复做的事、植物天生的长法，或修士常穿的袍子。

normal.en: Getting up early is his habit.
The plant has a climbing habit.
normal.cn: 这种植物有攀爬的习性。

normal.en: The monk wore a simple habit.
She broke the habit of biting her nails.
normal.cn: 她改掉了咬指甲的习惯。

normal.en: Good eating habits start young.
normal.cn: 良好的饮食习惯从小养成。

abstract.en: What we repeat quietly becomes who we are.
abstract.cn: 我们默默重复的事，成了我们自己。

abstract.en: A habit is a path worn smooth by walking.
abstract.cn: 习惯，是被走平的一条小路。

abstract.en: Even a plant has its own way of standing.
abstract.cn: 就连植物，也有自己站立的方式。

examples.en: Getting up early is his habit.
The plant has a climbing habit.
examples.cn: 这种植物有攀爬的习性。

examples.en: The monk wore a simple habit.

dict_mnemonic.text: habit 是「习惯」，也指动植物的「习性」和修士的「道袍」；break the habit 是戒掉习惯，out of habit 是出于习惯。

root: 来自拉丁语 habitus（状况；衣着），源于 habere（拥有）；反复持有的行为成为习惯，持有的衣着成为袍服，动植物的固有方式成为习性。

sensesIntro.en: Habit means a repeated action, a natural behaviour, or a religious garment.
sensesIntro.cn: habit 指反复的行为、天然的习性，或宗教袍服。

core.en: A way of being held and repeated.
core.cn: 被保持下来并反复的方式。

branches.en: A man reaches for the same cup each morning.
branches.cn: 男人每天早晨伸手拿同一个杯子。

branches.en: A vine climbs the same wall each year.
branches.cn: 藤蔓每年爬向同一面墙。

branches.en: A monk folds a long robe.
People and plants both keep to a pattern.
branches.cn: 人与植物，都守着一种模式。

branches.en: A repeated act and a worn dress are both held close.
branches.cn: 反复的行为与常穿的袍子，都被贴身保有。

intro.en: Habit forms adjectives, adverbs, and verbs of becoming used to something.
intro.cn: habit 构成形容词、副词，以及表示逐渐习惯的动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin habitus comes from habere, to have.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habitus 来自 habere（拥有）。

items.example: The habit is hard to break.
She is a habitual early riser.
They habituate the body to cold.
The animals were habituated to people.

items.meaningCN: 易成瘾的；易养成习惯的

latinEntries.exampleCN: habitus 进入英语后成为 habit。

latinEntries.example: Habere is the base of habitus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: habere 是 habitus 的词基。

definition_en: the fine threads that grow on the head or body, or a very small amount
core_image: 一根从头顶长出的细丝
scene: 她的头发又黑又长。Her hair is long and black.
sceneCN: 这里 hair 是「头发」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的头发又黑又长。

senses.title: Head hair
senses.definition: the fine threads that grow on a person's head
senses.definitionCN: 长在人头上的细丝
senses.example: Her hair is long and black.
senses.why: Hair on the head is the most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 头上的毛发，是最常见的义项。

senses.title: Body thread
senses.definition: a fine thread that grows on the body or skin of an animal
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物皮肤上长出的细丝
senses.example: The cat left hairs on the chair.
senses.why: The same word names a single body thread.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也指单根的体毛。

senses.title: Tiny amount
senses.definition: a very small amount or distance
senses.definitionCN: 极小的量或距离
senses.example: The ball missed by a hair.
senses.why: The width of a hair became a measure of smallness.
senses.whyCN: 一根头发的宽度，成了细微的尺度。

intro.en: Hair comes from Old English hær, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: hair 来自古英语 hær，源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root named hair or a fine thread.
items.cn: 该词根指毛发或细丝。

items.en: Hær meant hair on the head or body.
items.cn: hær 指头上或身上的毛。

items.en: Hair kept the same sense.
items.cn: hair 保留了同样的含义。

items.en: It named a single thread as well as the mass.
items.cn: 它既指一头毛发，也指单根毛发。

items.en: A hair's width became a figure for a tiny amount.
items.cn: 一根发的宽度，成为极小量的说法。

note.en: Hair is compared with look-alike words and words for strands and fur.
note.cn: 把 hair 与形近词以及表示细丝与兽毛的词作比较。

entries.definition: an animal like a large rabbit
the soft hair of an animal

normalIntro.en: Hair is the mass on the head, one thread on the body, or a measure of almost nothing.
normalIntro.cn: hair 是头上的整片毛发、身上的一根细丝，或近乎没有的微小尺度。

normal.en: Her hair is long and black.
The cat left hairs on the chair.
The ball missed by a hair.
He brushes his hair every morning.
She has fair hair and blue eyes.

abstract.en: A single thread can cover a whole head.
abstract.cn: 一根细丝，能覆盖整个头顶。

abstract.en: The smallest measure still decides a race.
abstract.cn: 最小的尺度，仍能决定一场比赛。

abstract.en: What grows without effort still marks us.
abstract.cn: 不费力长出的东西，仍留下我们的印记。

examples.en: Her hair is long and black.
The cat left hairs on the chair.
The ball missed by a hair.

dict_mnemonic.text: hair 是「头发」，也指「毛发」，还表示「毫厘」之微；hair loss 是脱发，a hair's breadth 是毫厘之差，hairy 是多毛的。

root: 来自古英语 hær（毛发），源于日耳曼语词根；由头上身上的细丝，引申为单根毛发，再比喻极小的距离与数量。

sensesIntro.en: Hair means the threads on the head, a body thread, or a very small amount.
sensesIntro.cn: hair 指头上的毛发、身上的一根毛，或极小的量。

core.en: A fine thread growing from skin.

branches.en: A brush passes through long hair.

senses.title: Middle of a process

senses.title: Compromise position

items.en: Healf meant half.

examples.en: It began to rain halfway there.

intro.cn: handbag 构成复数与表示大小的形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; hand is Germanic and bag is Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根；hand 属日耳曼语，bag 来自古诺斯语。

items.example: She has a large handbag collection.

items.meaning: a bag worn on the shoulder

definition_en: to deal with a situation, to operate something, the part of an object made to be held, or to touch with the hands
core_image: 一只手握住门把转动
scene: 她处理问题很冷静。She handled the problem calmly.
sceneCN: 这里 handle 是「处理」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她处理问题很冷静。

senses.title: Deal with
senses.definition: to deal with a situation, problem, or person
senses.definitionCN: 应对情况、问题或人
senses.example: She handled the problem calmly.
senses.why: Dealing with matters is the central modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 处理事务，是核心的现代义项。

senses.title: Operate
senses.definition: to use or control a machine or tool
senses.definitionCN: 使用或控制机器或工具
senses.example: He knows how to handle the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。
senses.why: To handle a thing is to make it work with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 操作一件东西，就是用手让它运转。

senses.title: Grip part
senses.definition: the part of an object made for the hand to hold
senses.definitionCN: 器物上供手握的部分
senses.example: The handle of the cup is broken.
senses.why: The noun names the place the hand takes.
senses.whyCN: 名词指手所握的位置。

senses.title: Touch
senses.definition: to touch or hold something with your hands
senses.definitionCN: 用手触摸或拿着某物
senses.example: Wash your hands after handling raw meat.
senses.why: The oldest sense is feeling something with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项，是用手去感触。

intro.en: Handle comes from Old English handlian, to feel or touch with the hands, from hand.
intro.cn: handle 来自古英语 handlian（用手触摸），源于 hand。

items.en: Handlian meant to touch or use with the hands.
items.cn: handlian 意为用手触摸或使用。

items.en: Handlen meant to touch or deal with.
items.cn: handlen 意为触摸或处理。

items.en: Handle named the part made for the hand.
items.cn: handle 指为手而设的部分。

items.en: It came to mean managing a situation.
items.cn: 它转而表示应对局面。

items.en: It also meant operating a machine.
items.cn: 它也指操作机器。

note.en: Handle is compared with look-alike words and words for dealing with things.
note.cn: 把 handle 与形近词以及表示应付事物的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To handle is to take something in hand, whether a problem, a machine, or a cup.
normalIntro.cn: handle 就是把东西拿在手里，无论是问题、机器还是一只杯子。

normal.en: She handled the problem calmly.
He knows how to handle the machine.
normal.cn: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。

normal.en: The handle of the cup is broken.
Wash your hands after handling raw meat.
Handle the box with care.

abstract.en: To handle a thing is to accept its weight.
abstract.cn: 拿起一件东西，就是接受它的重量。

abstract.en: A handle is a promise that the hand belongs there.
abstract.cn: 把手是一种承诺：手该放在这里。

abstract.en: The calm hand steadies the whole room.
abstract.cn: 沉稳的手，稳住整间屋子。

examples.en: She handled the problem calmly.
He knows how to handle the machine.
examples.cn: 他知道怎样操作这台机器。

examples.en: The handle of the cup is broken.

dict_mnemonic.text: handle 是「处理、操作」，也指「触摸」，名词是「把手」；handle a problem 是处理问题，handle with care 是小心轻放，door handle 是门把手。

root: 来自古英语 handlian（用手触摸），源于 hand；用手去碰、去用，引申为操作与处理，又指为手而设的把手。

sensesIntro.en: Handle means to deal with, to operate, a grip part, or to touch with the hands.
sensesIntro.cn: handle 指处理、操作、把手，或用手触摸。

core.en: The hand taking hold of a thing.
core.cn: 手抓住一件东西。

branches.en: A manager calms a difficult meeting.
branches.cn: 管理者稳住一场棘手的会议。

branches.en: A worker turns a control wheel.
A hand closes on a door grip.
Fingers touch a rough surface.
The grip part and the act of dealing both begin with the hand.
branches.cn: 把手与处理，都从手开始。

intro.en: Handle forms verbs, agent nouns, and compounds of holding.
intro.cn: handle 构成动词、施动者名词，以及表示握持的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word comes from Old English hand.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，源自英语 hand（古英语）。

items.meaning: the bar used to steer a bicycle

definition_en: useful and easy to use, kept near at hand, or good at using your hands
core_image: 工具箱放在伸手可及的地方
scene: 这把小刀很方便携带。This small knife is handy to carry.
sceneCN: 这里 handy 是「便利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这把小刀很方便携带。

senses.title: Easy to use
senses.definition: useful and easy to use
senses.definitionCN: 有用且容易使用
senses.example: This small knife is handy to carry.
senses.why: Usefulness with ease is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 好用又省力，是中心义项。

senses.title: Near at hand
senses.definition: kept near and ready to be used
senses.definitionCN: 放在近处、随时可用
senses.example: Keep the torch handy in case of a power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 把手电放在手边，以防停电。
senses.why: Nearness to the hand is part of being handy.
senses.whyCN: 在手边，是 handy 含义的一部分。

senses.title: Skilled with hands
senses.definition: good at making or repairing things with your hands
senses.definitionCN: 擅长用手制作或修理东西
senses.example: She is handy with tools.
senses.why: A skilled hand also earns this word.
senses.whyCN: 灵巧的手，也配得上这个词。

intro.en: Handy is hand plus the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: handy 由 hand 加形容词词尾 -y 构成。

items.en: Hand meant the hand.
items.cn: hand 意为手。

items.en: Handy meant done or used by hand.
items.cn: handy 意为用手做的或用手使用的。

items.en: It came to mean easy to use.
items.cn: 它转而表示容易使用。

items.en: It meant kept near at hand.
items.cn: 它表示放在手边。

items.en: It also meant skilled with the hands.
items.cn: 它也指双手灵巧。

note.en: Handy is compared with look-alike words and words for convenience and skill.
note.cn: 把 handy 与形近词以及表示便利与灵巧的词作比较。

entries.definition: the body part at the end of the arm

normalIntro.en: Handy means close to the hand, easy to use, or skilled in the use of hands.
normalIntro.cn: handy 指就在手边、使用方便，或双手灵巧。

normal.en: This small knife is handy to carry.
Keep the torch handy in case of a power cut.
normal.cn: 把手电放在手边，以防停电。

normal.en: She is handy with tools.
A pocket dictionary comes in handy.
The box is handy for storing letters.
normal.cn: 这个盒子用来收纳信件很方便。

abstract.en: What is near the hand is quickly part of the mind.
abstract.cn: 手边的东西，很快成为心智的一部分。

abstract.en: A good tool disappears into its use.
abstract.cn: 好用的工具，会消失在使用之中。

abstract.en: Skilled hands make difficulty look quiet.
abstract.cn: 灵巧的手，让困难显得安静。

examples.en: This small knife is handy to carry.
Keep the torch handy in case of a power cut.
examples.cn: 把手电放在手边，以防停电。

examples.en: She is handy with tools.

dict_mnemonic.text: handy 由 hand 加 -y 构成，意为「便利的、手边的、手巧的」；come in handy 是派得上用场，keep handy 是放在手边。

root: 由 hand（手）加形容词词尾 -y 构成；与手有关，引申为就在手边、用起来方便，以及双手灵巧。

sensesIntro.en: Handy means easy to use, near at hand, or skilled with the hands.
sensesIntro.cn: handy 指便于使用、就在手边，或双手灵巧。

core.en: Within easy reach of the hand.
core.cn: 伸手就能触及。

branches.en: A small tool fits a pocket.
branches.cn: 一件小工具刚好放进衣袋。

branches.en: A torch waits by the door.
A repairer turns a screw with ease.
Easy use begins with being near.
branches.cn: 好用的前提，是就在近处。

branches.en: What is near is quickly handled by skilled hands.
branches.cn: 近处的东西，很快被灵巧的手用上。

intro.en: Handy forms comparison, adverbs, nouns, and compounds of skill.
intro.cn: handy 构成比较级、副词、名词，以及表示手艺的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word comes from Old English hand.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，源自英语 hand（古英语）。

items.meaning: a person who does small repairs

definition_en: to take place, to do something by chance, or to find something by chance
core_image: 路口突然响起刹车声
scene: 事故发生在十字路口。The accident happened at the crossing.
sceneCN: 这里 happen 是「发生」（第 1 个义项）；句意：事故发生在十字路口。

senses.title: Take place
senses.definition: to take place, especially without being planned
senses.definitionCN: 发生，尤指未事先计划地发生
senses.example: The accident happened at the crossing.
senses.why: An event taking place is the central sense.
senses.whyCN: 事件发生，是中心义项。

senses.title: By chance
senses.definition: to do something by chance
senses.definitionCN: 碰巧做了某事
senses.example: I happened to meet her at the station.
senses.why: Chance became a word for a lucky coincidence.
senses.whyCN: 偶然，成了表示巧合的说法。

senses.title: Come upon
senses.definition: to find or meet something by chance
senses.definitionCN: 偶然发现或遇到某事
senses.example: He happened on an old letter.
senses.why: Finding by chance is the same idea in another form.
senses.whyCN: 偶然发现，是同一概念的另一形式。

intro.en: Happen comes from hap, chance, from Old Norse happ, plus the verb ending -en.
intro.cn: happen 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、偶然），加动词词尾 -en 构成。

items.en: Happ meant chance or good luck.
items.cn: happ 意为偶然或好运。

items.en: Hap named a chance event.
items.cn: hap 指偶然事件。

items.en: Happen meant to take place by chance.
items.cn: happen 意为偶然发生。

items.en: It extended to any event taking place.
items.cn: 它扩展到任何事件的发生。

items.en: It also meant meeting or finding by chance.
items.cn: 它也指偶然遇到或发现。

note.en: Happen is compared with look-alike words and words for events and chance.
note.cn: 把 happen 与形近词以及表示事件与偶然的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Happen is what chance brings: an event takes place, or two people meet by luck.
normalIntro.cn: happen 是偶然带来的事：事件发生，或两人碰巧相遇。

normal.en: The accident happened at the crossing.
I happened to meet her at the station.
He happened on an old letter.
What happened to your bike?
It will not happen again.

abstract.en: Chance is the part of life no plan can hold.
abstract.cn: 偶然，是任何计划都握不住的那部分生活。

abstract.en: What happens is not always what is chosen.
abstract.cn: 发生的事，不总是被选择的事。

abstract.en: A chance meeting can change a whole road.
abstract.cn: 一次偶遇，能改变整条路。

examples.en: The accident happened at the crossing.
I happened to meet her at the station.
He happened on an old letter.

dict_mnemonic.text: happen 是「发生」，也指「碰巧」和「偶然遇到」；happen to 是碰巧或发生在……身上，what happened 是发生了什么。

root: 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、偶然），加动词词尾 -en；偶然降临之事，引申为发生、碰巧与偶然遇见。

sensesIntro.en: Happen means to take place, to do something by chance, or to find something by chance.
sensesIntro.cn: happen 指发生、碰巧做某事，或偶然发现某物。

core.en: An event arriving out of chance.
core.cn: 由偶然带来的一件事。

branches.en: A car stops at a crossing.
Two friends meet by accident.
A letter slips from an old book.
An event and a meeting both arrive by chance.
branches.cn: 事件与相遇，都因偶然到来。

branches.en: Something found and something occurring share the same luck.
branches.cn: 发现与发生，共享同一种运气。

intro.en: Happen forms verb parts, event nouns, and chance compounds.
intro.cn: happen 构成动词变化、事件名词，以及表示偶然的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; hap comes from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，hap 来自古诺斯语。

items.exampleCN: 他们偶然发现一处泉水。

definition_en: feeling pleased and content, or willing to do something
core_image: 一个孩子接到礼物时笑弯了眼睛
scene: 她收到礼物时很开心。She was happy when she got the gift.
sceneCN: 这里 happy 是「高兴的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她收到礼物时很开心。

senses.title: Glad about something
senses.definition: feeling pleasure about something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 因发生某事而感到愉快
senses.example: She was happy when she got the gift.
senses.why: This is the everyday feeling sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的情绪义项。

senses.title: Content in life
senses.definition: satisfied with life and not troubled
senses.definitionCN: 对生活满足而无忧
senses.example: They live a happy life in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在乡下过着幸福的生活。
senses.why: The feeling lasts long enough to become a life.
senses.whyCN: 情绪持续得够久，就成了一种生活。

senses.title: Willing
senses.definition: willing and glad to do something
senses.definitionCN: 愿意并乐于去做某事
senses.example: I am happy to help.
senses.why: A pleased mind says yes more easily.
senses.whyCN: 愉快的心，更容易说行。

intro.en: Happy comes from the noun hap, luck or chance, plus the ending -y.
intro.cn: happy 由名词 hap（运气、机缘）加后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Happ meant luck or chance.
items.cn: happ 意为运气或机缘。

items.en: Hap named good fortune.
items.cn: hap 指好运。

items.en: Happy meant favoured by luck.
items.cn: happy 意为受到幸运眷顾的。

items.en: The sense moved to inner pleasure.
items.cn: 词义转向内心的愉悦。

items.en: Happy also came to mean willing.
items.cn: happy 也引申为「乐意」。

note.en: Happy is compared with look-alike words and with words for good feeling.
note.cn: 把 happy 与形近词以及表示良好感受的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Happy began as good luck and became a warm feeling inside.
normalIntro.cn: happy 起初指好运气，后来变成心里的一股暖意。

normal.en: Happy birthday to you.
She looks happy today.
They had a happy childhood.
I am happy to wait.
He is happy with the result.

abstract.en: Luck was once the whole of happiness.
abstract.cn: 曾经，运气就是全部的幸福。

abstract.en: A happy face is a door left open.
abstract.cn: 一张笑脸，是一扇开着的门。

abstract.en: To say yes gladly is its own small joy.
abstract.cn: 乐意说「好」，本身就是小小的快乐。

examples.en: She was happy when she got the gift.
They live a happy life in the country.
examples.cn: 他们在乡下过着幸福的生活。

examples.en: I am happy to help.

dict_mnemonic.text: happy 由 hap（运气）加 -y 构成，本指「走运」，后指内心的「高兴、幸福」；be happy to 是乐意做，happy ending 是圆满结局。

root: 来自古诺斯语 happ（运气、机缘），加形容词后缀 -y；由「受幸运眷顾」引申为内心的愉悦、生活的幸福与做事的乐意。

sensesIntro.en: Happy describes a glad moment, a contented life, or a willing yes.
sensesIntro.cn: happy 描述一时的高兴、一生的幸福，或乐意的一句应允。

core.en: A face that has just relaxed into a smile.
core.cn: 一张刚刚舒展成笑的脸。

branches.en: A parcel opens and eyes grow bright.
A family eats together every evening.
branches.cn: 一家人每天傍晚一起吃饭。

branches.en: A hand rises before the request ends.
branches.cn: 请求还没说完，手就举了起来。

branches.en: Small glad moments build a happy life.
branches.cn: 一个个小高兴，垒成幸福的一生。

branches.en: A glad heart says yes first.
branches.cn: 愉快的心，总是先说出「好」。

intro.en: Happy takes comparison and forms a noun, an adverb, and a negative form.
intro.cn: happy 加比较级，并构成名词、副词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word comes from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，来自古诺斯语。

items.example: He was unhappy with the plan.

items.meaning: a good end to a story
items.example: The film has a happy ending.

items.exampleCN: 他们在优惠时段见了面。

definition_zh: 硬的；困难的；努力的；猛烈地
definition_en: firm and solid, difficult to do, or using a lot of effort
core_image: 拳头敲在硬木桌面上发出闷响
scene: 这张床太硬，睡不舒服。The bed is too hard to sleep on.
sceneCN: 这里 hard 是「硬的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这张床太硬，睡不舒服。

senses.title: Firm to the touch
senses.definition: firm and solid and not easily pressed or bent
senses.definitionCN: 坚实而不易按压或弯曲的
senses.example: The bed is too hard to sleep on.
senses.why: This is the physical material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是材料层面的物理义项。

senses.title: Difficult
senses.definition: difficult to do or to understand
senses.definitionCN: 难以做到或理解的
senses.example: It is hard to say.
senses.why: A hard surface resists the hand, as a hard task resists effort.
senses.whyCN: 硬的表面抗拒手，难的任务抗拒努力。

senses.title: Full of effort
senses.definition: showing or needing a lot of effort and energy
senses.definitionCN: 付出或需要大量精力与努力的
senses.example: He is a hard worker.
senses.why: What resists you must be pushed hard.
senses.whyCN: 抗拒你的东西，必须用力去推。

senses.title: With force
senses.definition: with great effort or force, as an adverb
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指用力或猛烈地
senses.example: It rained hard all night.
senses.why: The adverb keeps the idea of force.
senses.whyCN: 副词形式保留了「用力」的意思。

intro.en: Hard comes from Old English heard, firm or severe.
intro.cn: hard 来自古英语 heard，意为坚实或严厉。

items.en: The root meant firm and strong.
items.cn: 该词根意为坚实、强壮。

items.en: Heard described a hard surface.
items.cn: heard 描述坚硬的表面。

items.en: Hard extended to difficult tasks.
items.cn: hard 扩展到困难的任务。

items.en: It also praised steady effort.
items.cn: 它也用来称赞持续的努力。

items.en: The adverb sense grew alongside.
items.cn: 副词义也随之发展。

note.en: Hard is compared with look-alike words and with words for firmness and difficulty.
note.cn: 把 hard 与形近词以及表示坚硬和困难的词作比较。

entries.definition: able to live in hard conditions
an animal like a large rabbit

normalIntro.en: Hard is a wall under the hand, a task against the will, and the force you answer with.
normalIntro.cn: hard 是手下的一面墙，是挡在意志前的一件难事，也是你回敬它的那股力。

normal.en: The ground is hard and dry.
This question is hard.
She works hard every day.
It rained hard last night.
He tried hard to win.

abstract.en: What is hard teaches the hand its strength.
abstract.cn: 坚硬的东西，教会手它的力量。

abstract.en: A hard road is still a road.
abstract.cn: 难走的路，仍然是路。

abstract.en: Effort is the answer a hard world asks for.
abstract.cn: 努力，是坚硬的世界索要的答案。

examples.en: The bed is too hard to sleep on.
It is hard to say.
It rained hard all night.

dict_mnemonic.text: hard 本义是「硬的」，引申为「困难的」「努力的」；作副词是「努力地、猛烈地」，如 work hard、rain hard；注意 hardly 意思完全不同，是「几乎不」。

root: 来自古英语 heard（坚实、严厉），源于日耳曼语；由坚固的表面，引申为难以对付的任务，再引申为用力与勤勉。

sensesIntro.en: Hard describes a solid surface, a difficult task, steady effort, or force in action.
sensesIntro.cn: hard 描述坚实的表面、困难的任务、持续的努力，或动作中的力量。

core.en: A surface that resists the hand.
core.cn: 抗拒手掌的表面。

branches.en: Knuckles knock on a wooden table.
A question has no ready answer.
branches.cn: 一个问题没有现成答案。

branches.en: A lamp stays on past midnight.
Rain beats against a window.
A hard task is met with hard work.

intro.en: Hard takes comparison and builds adverbs, verbs, and nouns of effort.
intro.cn: hard 加比较级，并构成副词、动词与表示艰难的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The hardness of the wood helps.

definition_en: almost not at all, or only just
core_image: 一束几乎看不见的微光
scene: 他几乎听不见她的声音。He could hardly hear her voice.
sceneCN: 这里 hardly 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他几乎听不见她的声音。

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: to almost no degree at all
senses.definitionCN: 程度几乎为零
senses.example: He could hardly hear her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最主要的意思。

senses.title: Surely not
senses.definition: used to say that something is very unlikely or unsuitable
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事极不可能或不合适
senses.example: That is hardly a fair answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那简直算不上公平的回答。
senses.why: The same smallness turns into doubt.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「极少」，转成了怀疑。

senses.title: Only just
senses.definition: only a moment ago
senses.definitionCN: 只在片刻之前
senses.example: I had hardly arrived when it rained.
senses.why: An older sense of barely in time.
senses.whyCN: 这是「时间上刚好」的古老义项。

intro.en: Hardly is hard plus -ly, which first meant with force and later almost not.
intro.cn: hardly 是 hard 加 -ly，最初意为「用力地」，后转为「几乎不」。

items.en: Heard meant firm.
items.cn: heard 意为坚实。

items.en: Hardly meant with force.
items.cn: hardly 意为用力地。

items.en: The sense shifted to barely.
items.cn: 词义转向「勉强、几乎不」。

items.en: Hardly ever became a common phrase.
items.cn: hardly ever 成为常用搭配。

items.en: Hardly also marked things almost untrue.
items.cn: hardly 也用来表示「简直不」。

note.en: Hardly is compared with look-alike words and with words of small degree.
note.cn: 把 hardly 与形近词以及表示微小程度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hardly looks like hard but means almost not, a small light on the edge of seeing.
normalIntro.cn: hardly 看着像 hard，意思却是「几乎不」，像视野边缘的一点微光。

normal.en: I can hardly believe it.
She hardly eats meat.
He hardly ever calls.
There is hardly any water left.
I had hardly sat down when the phone rang.

abstract.en: What is hardly there still asks to be noticed.
abstract.cn: 几乎不存在的东西，仍然渴望被看见。

abstract.en: Hard work and hardly working are a letter apart.
abstract.cn: 努力工作与几乎不做，只差一个字母。

abstract.en: Almost nothing is still something.
abstract.cn: 几乎什么都没有，也还是有一点。

examples.en: He could hardly hear her voice.
examples.cn: 他几乎听不见她的声音。

examples.en: That is hardly a fair answer.
examples.cn: 那简直算不上公平的回答。

examples.en: I had hardly arrived when it rained.

dict_mnemonic.text: hardly 虽是 hard 加 -ly，意思却不是「努力地」，而是「几乎不」；hardly ever 是几乎从不，hardly any 是几乎没有，hardly...when 是刚一……就。

root: hard（用力、艰难）加 -ly；中古英语本指「用力地」，后词义转为「勉强、几乎不」与「简直不」。

sensesIntro.en: Hardly means almost not, surely not, or only just.
sensesIntro.cn: hardly 指几乎不、简直不，或刚刚才。

core.en: A light too faint to be sure of.
core.cn: 弱得让人不敢确定的一点光。

branches.en: A voice fades at the far end of a hall.
An excuse does not hold up.
A door closes just as a knock comes.
branches.cn: 门刚关上，敲门声就响了。

branches.en: What is almost nothing is also almost untrue.
branches.cn: 几乎为零的东西，也几乎不成立。

branches.en: A bare moment is a small amount of time.
branches.cn: 「刚刚」不过是极少的一点时间。

intro.en: Hardly is fixed in form, built from hard and -ly.
intro.cn: hardly 形式固定，由 hard 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: Test the hardness of the stone.

definition_en: damage or injury to a person or thing, or to cause such damage
core_image: 一只脚踩坏了刚刚长出的嫩芽
scene: 吸烟会伤害身体。Smoking can harm your health.
sceneCN: 这里 harm 是「伤害」（第 3 个义项，动词）；句意：吸烟会伤害身体。

senses.title: Injury to the body
senses.definition: physical injury or damage to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 对人畜造成的身体损伤
senses.example: The fall did him no harm.
senses.why: This is the basic injury sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的损伤义项。

senses.title: Damage to interests
senses.definition: damage to something valuable, such as trust or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对信任、名誉等有价值之物的破坏
senses.example: The rumour harmed her reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 那则谣言损害了她的名誉。
senses.why: What can hurt a body can hurt a name.
senses.whyCN: 能伤身体的，也能伤名声。

senses.title: Cause damage
senses.definition: to cause damage or injury to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物造成损伤或破坏
senses.example: Smoking can harm your health.
senses.why: The noun of damage became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 损害的名词，转成了动词。

intro.en: Harm comes from Old English hearm, injury or grief.
intro.cn: harm 来自古英语 hearm，意为伤害或悲痛。

items.en: The root meant injury.
items.cn: 该词根意为损伤。

items.en: Hearm meant harm or sorrow.
items.cn: hearm 意为伤害或悲伤。

items.en: Harm named damage of any kind.
items.cn: harm 指任何形式的损害。

items.en: The verb sense of injuring grew.
items.cn: 「使受伤」的动词义发展起来。

items.en: The phrase no harm done became common.
items.cn: no harm done 成为常用说法。

note.en: Harm is compared with look-alike words and with words for damage and injury.
note.cn: 把 harm 与形近词以及表示损害和伤害的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harm is a foot on a young shoot, a word on a good name, and an action against a body.
normalIntro.cn: harm 是踩在新芽上的一只脚，是落在好名声上的一句话，也是加在身体上的一个动作。

normal.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.
The storm did little harm.
No harm done, so let us go on.
normal.cn: 没造成伤害，我们继续吧。

normal.en: The law protects animals from harm.
normal.cn: 法律保护动物免受伤害。

normal.en: He meant no harm.

abstract.en: What is done in a moment can harm for years.
abstract.cn: 一瞬间做的事，能伤害很多年。

abstract.en: The softest words can leave the deepest marks.
abstract.cn: 最软的话，能留下最深的痕。

abstract.en: To mean no harm is not the same as doing none.
abstract.cn: 没有恶意，不等于没有伤害。

examples.en: Smoking can harm your health.
The rumour harmed her reputation.
examples.cn: 那则谣言损害了她的名誉。

examples.en: The fall did him no harm.

dict_mnemonic.text: harm 可作名词也可作动词，都是「伤害、损害」；do harm to 是对……有害，no harm done 是没造成伤害，harm the environment 是损害环境。

root: 来自古英语 hearm（伤害、悲伤），源于日耳曼语；由身体的损伤，引申为名誉、利益与环境所受的破坏。

sensesIntro.en: Harm is injury to a body, damage to something valued, or the act of causing either.
sensesIntro.cn: harm 是对身体的损伤、对有价值之物的破坏，或造成这两者的行为。

core.en: A blow that leaves a mark.
core.cn: 留下痕迹的一击。

branches.en: A knee hits stone and swells.
branches.cn: 膝盖撞上石头，肿了起来。

branches.en: A false story spreads through a town.
branches.cn: 一个假消息在小镇传开。

branches.en: Smoke enters a pair of lungs.
An injury and an injuring act are one event.
branches.cn: 伤与致伤的动作，是同一件事。

branches.en: A body and a reputation bruise the same way.
branches.cn: 身体与名誉，受伤的方式一样。

intro.en: Harm takes verb endings and forms two contrasting adjectives with -ful and -less.
intro.cn: harm 加动词词尾，并用 -ful 与 -less 构成两个相对形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The waste was disposed of harmfully.
items.exampleCN: 这些废物被有害地处理了。

definition_en: a covering worn on the head, or a role a person takes on
core_image: 一顶宽檐草帽挂在门边的钩子上
scene: 她戴着一顶草帽。She wore a straw hat.
sceneCN: 这里 hat 是「帽子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她戴着一顶草帽。

senses.title: Head covering
senses.definition: a shaped covering worn on the head
senses.definitionCN: 戴在头上的成形覆盖物
senses.example: She wore a straw hat.
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: A role at work
senses.definition: one of several roles or duties a person has
senses.definitionCN: 一个人承担的多个角色或职责之一
senses.example: He wears two hats in the company.
senses.why: Changing a hat became changing a role.
senses.whyCN: 换一顶帽子，就变成换一个角色。

senses.title: Sign of status
senses.definition: a hat as a sign of a person's rank or office
senses.definitionCN: 作为级别或职务标志的帽子
senses.example: The captain's hat marks his rank.
senses.exampleCN: 船长的帽子标明他的级别。
senses.why: A uniform hat is a badge you can wear.
senses.whyCN: 制服帽是能戴在身上的徽章。

intro.en: Hat comes from Old English hæt, a head covering.
intro.cn: hat 来自古英语 hæt，指头部覆盖物。

items.en: The root named a head covering.
items.cn: 该词根指头部覆盖物。

items.en: Hæt meant a hat or hood.
items.cn: hæt 指帽子或头巾。

items.en: Hat named the modern shaped hat.
items.cn: hat 指现代成形的帽子。

items.en: Hats marked rank and uniform.
items.cn: 帽子标示级别与制服。

items.en: Wearing hats came to mean roles.
items.cn: 戴帽子引申为承担角色。

note.en: Hat is compared with look-alike words and with words for headwear and roles.
note.cn: 把 hat 与形近词以及表示头饰和角色的词作比较。

entries.definition: a soft hat with a peak
a part played by a person

normalIntro.en: A hat covers a head, marks a rank, and stands for the role you are playing.
normalIntro.cn: hat 罩住一颗头，标明一个级别，也代表你正在扮演的角色。

normal.en: Put on your hat, it is cold.
He tipped his hat to the lady.
normal.cn: 他向那位女士抬帽致意。

normal.en: She scored a hat trick.
I take off my hat to your courage.
He wears the hat of a teacher.

abstract.en: A hat is a small roof you carry with you.
abstract.cn: 帽子，是一小片随身携带的屋顶。

abstract.en: Change the hat and you change the voice.
abstract.cn: 换一顶帽子，就换一种语气。

abstract.en: Some hats are worn and some hats are earned.
abstract.cn: 有些帽子是戴上的，有些帽子是挣来的。

examples.en: She wore a straw hat.
He wears two hats in the company.
The captain's hat marks his rank.
examples.cn: 船长的帽子标明他的级别。

dict_mnemonic.text: hat 是「帽子」；hat trick 是帽子戏法，take off one's hat to 是向……致敬，wear many hats 是身兼多职，因为换一顶帽子就换一种身份。

root: 来自古英语 hæt（头巾、帽子）；由头部覆盖物，引申为制服所标示的级别，再引申为人所承担的角色与职责。

sensesIntro.en: Hat is a head covering, a role at work, or a sign of rank.
sensesIntro.cn: hat 是头部覆盖物、工作中的角色，或级别的标志。

core.en: A shape that sits on a head.
core.cn: 一个落在头上的形状。

branches.en: A straw hat hangs by the door.
One worker answers two kinds of calls.
A white cap marks the captain.
A uniform hat is clothing and badge at once.
branches.cn: 制服帽，既是衣物也是徽章。

branches.en: The hat you wear says who is speaking.
branches.cn: 你戴的帽子，说明是谁在说话。

intro.en: Hat takes a plural and forms compounds and phrases of headwear.
intro.cn: hat 加复数，并构成头饰类复合词与短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: He walked hatless in the sun.

items.meaning: as much as a hat holds

items.example: She is used to wearing hats.

definition_en: to dislike someone or something very strongly
core_image: 攥紧的拳头和咬紧的牙关
scene: 她讨厌撒谎的人。She hates liars.
sceneCN: 这里 hate 是「讨厌、憎恨」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她讨厌撒谎的人。

senses.title: Dislike a thing
senses.definition: to dislike an activity or thing very much
senses.definitionCN: 非常不喜欢某项活动或某样东西
senses.example: I hate cold mornings.
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of strong dislike.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表达强烈厌恶的义项。

senses.title: Feel hostility
senses.definition: to feel strong dislike toward a person
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有强烈的厌恶
senses.example: She hates liars.
senses.why: The feeling turns from a thing to a person.
senses.whyCN: 这种情绪从对事物转向对人。

senses.title: The feeling itself
senses.definition: a strong feeling of dislike kept inside
senses.definitionCN: 积在心中的强烈厌恶情绪
senses.example: His face was full of hate.
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun for the emotion.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示这种情感的名词。

intro.en: Hate goes back to an Old English verb for strong dislike.
intro.cn: hate 可追溯到古英语中表示强烈厌恶的动词。

items.en: The root expressed strong dislike.
items.cn: 该词根表达强烈的厌恶。

items.en: Old English hatian meant to hate.
items.cn: 古英语 hatian 意为憎恨。

items.en: Hate named the feeling as well as the act.
items.cn: hate 既指行为也指情感。

items.en: Hate became a strong word for dislike.
items.cn: hate 成为表达厌恶的强词。

items.en: Hate speech named words that stir hostility.
items.cn: 仇恨言论一词用来指煽动敌意的言辞。

note.en: Hate is compared with look-alike words and with words for strong dislike.
note.cn: 把 hate 与形近词以及表示强烈厌恶的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hate is a hot feeling that turns against people or things.
normalIntro.cn: hate 是一种烧向人或物的强烈情绪。

normal.en: I hate getting up early.
She hates being lied to.
They hate waste of any kind.
normal.cn: 他们痛恨任何形式的浪费。

normal.en: His eyes were full of hate.
Hate speech is banned here.

abstract.en: Hate is a fire that burns the one who holds it.
abstract.cn: 仇恨是烧向持火者自己的火。

abstract.en: Hate names the wound and keeps it open.
abstract.cn: 仇恨给伤口命名，还让它一直敞着。

abstract.en: The opposite of hate is not indifference but understanding.
abstract.cn: 恨的反面不是冷漠，而是理解。

examples.en: She hates liars.
I hate cold mornings.
His face was full of hate.

dict_mnemonic.text: hate 是「憎恨、讨厌」；hate to do 与 hate doing 都表示不愿做，hate speech 是仇恨言论，名词 hate 指仇恨这种情感。

root: 来自古英语 hatian（憎恨），与日耳曼语同源；由对人或物的强烈厌恶，发展为既可作动词也可作名词的仇恨。

sensesIntro.en: Hate is strong dislike for a thing, a person, or a group.
sensesIntro.cn: hate 是对事物、人或群体的强烈厌恶。

core.en: A hot feeling turned against someone.
core.cn: 一股转向某人的灼热情绪。

branches.en: I hate cold mornings.
She hates liars.
His face was full of hate.
The same feeling targets things and people.
branches.cn: 同一种情绪可以指向事物，也可以指向人。

branches.en: Hating a person hardens into hate.
branches.cn: 对人的憎恨，会硬化成仇恨。

intro.en: Hate takes endings and builds words about hating.
intro.cn: hate 加词尾，构成与憎恨相关的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: That was a hateful thing to say.
The law treats it as a hate crime.
items.exampleCN: 法律将其视为仇恨犯罪。

definition_en: to own something, to take part in an activity, to cause something, or to form the perfect tense
core_image: 双手紧紧握住一件属于自己的东西
scene: 我有两只猫。I have two cats.
sceneCN: 这里 have 是「拥有」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我有两只猫。

senses.title: Own or hold
senses.definition: to own or hold something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或持有某物
senses.example: I have two cats.
senses.why: This is the basic sense of possession.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示拥有的基本义项。

senses.title: Take part in
senses.definition: to eat, drink, or take part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 吃、喝或参加某项活动
senses.example: We have breakfast at seven.
senses.why: Possession stretches to doing things.
senses.whyCN: 「拥有」延伸为「做某事」。

senses.title: Form the perfect tense
senses.definition: used with a past participle to build the perfect tense
senses.definitionCN: 与过去分词连用，构成完成时
senses.example: She has finished her work.
senses.why: The verb thins into a grammar helper.
senses.whyCN: 这个词虚化为语法助词。

senses.title: Make something happen
senses.definition: to cause something to be done or to make someone act
senses.definitionCN: 使某事被做成，或让人去做
senses.example: I had my hair cut.
senses.why: Holding becomes arranging and ordering.
senses.whyCN: 「握在手里」变成了安排与支使。

intro.en: Have is an old Germanic verb for holding.
intro.cn: have 是一个古老的日耳曼语动词，意为持有。

items.en: The root meant to hold or possess.
items.cn: 该词根意为持有或拥有。

items.en: Habban meant to have or hold.
items.cn: habban 意为有或持有。

items.en: Have took its modern spelling.
items.cn: have 定型为现代拼写。

items.en: Have became an auxiliary for perfect tenses.
items.cn: have 成为构成完成时的助动词。

items.en: Have also meant to eat or to cause.
items.cn: have 也表示吃或使役。

note.en: Have is compared with look-alike words and with words for owning.
note.cn: 把 have 与形近词以及表示拥有的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Have holds things, takes actions, and builds perfect tenses.
normalIntro.cn: have 抓住东西、开展行动，也搭起完成时。

normal.en: I have a small garden.
We have lunch at noon.
She has two brothers.
They have finished the report.
I had my watch repaired.

abstract.en: To have is to hold, and to hold is to be responsible.
abstract.cn: 拥有就是握持，握持就是负责。

abstract.en: Have turns time into a single arc.
abstract.cn: have 把时间连成一道弧。

abstract.en: What we have says less than what we do.
abstract.cn: 我们拥有什么，不如我们做了什么。

examples.en: I have two cats.
We have breakfast at seven.
She has finished her work.

dict_mnemonic.text: have 是「有」；have to 是不得不，have a look 是看一看，have breakfast 是吃早饭，助动词 have 还能构成完成时。

root: 来自古英语 habban（持有），与日耳曼语同源；由「握在手里」引申为拥有、进行活动，再虚化为构成完成时的助动词。

sensesIntro.en: Have means to own, to take part in, to cause, or to form the perfect tense.
sensesIntro.cn: have 表示拥有、进行、使役，或构成完成时。

core.en: A hand closed around something.
core.cn: 一只手把某样东西握紧。

branches.en: I have two cats.
We have breakfast at seven.
She has finished her work.
I had my hair cut.
Holding a thing and making a thing happen.
branches.cn: 握住一样东西，也让一件事发生。

intro.en: Have changes form for person and tense and builds fixed phrases.
intro.cn: have 随人称与时态变形，并构成固定短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。
